comparison: Strong agreement on CRISPR-generated dmist allele (C61-C66). Both evaluations find the independent allele validation and behavioral phenotypes well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes molecular characterization and statistical rigor; peer reviewers praise the elegant CRISPR methodology.

Strong agreement on core dmist identification and sleep phenotypes (C3-C5, C37-C42). Both find behavioral data compelling with appropriate controls. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment; peer reviewers note 'elegant methods' and 'compelling evidence.'

Strong agreement on genetic interaction data (C94-C96). Both evaluations accept the epistatic relationship between dmist and atp1a3a. Peer reviewers explicitly list this as a strength. OpenEval notes the inference of direct interaction could benefit from biochemical evidence, but peer reviewers do not raise this concern.

Agreement on structural similarity to FXYD1 (C67-C69). Both accept the homology data. OpenEval appropriately labels C70 as speculation; peer reviewers accept the structural characterization without challenge.

Agreement on sodium measurements (C90-C92). Both evaluations accept the Sodium Green data showing elevated Na+ in mutants. OpenEval emphasizes the time-of-day specificity; peer reviewers accept findings as consistent with Na+/K+-ATPase defects.

Agreement on fxyd1 and atp1a3a sleep phenotypes (C73-C76). Both accept the data without challenge. OpenEval notes distinction in sleep architecture between fxyd1 and dmist; peer reviewers accept findings but question mechanistic implications of different expression patterns.

Divergent interpretations of PTZ homeostatic response (C93, C110). OpenEval finds the exaggerated sleep rebound well-supported and consistent with impaired Na+ pump function. Peer reviewer 1 explicitly states difficulty understanding this finding in context of decreased baseline sleep, marking it as a weakness.

Agreement on dmist expression and structural characterization (C51-C57 overlap). Both accept neuronal expression pattern and molecular features. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches; peer reviewers accept characterization without concerns.

Agreement on molecular characterization of dmist (C46-C50). Both evaluations accept RT-qPCR, computational predictions, and sequence data. OpenEval finds methodology thorough with appropriate controls; peer reviewers do not challenge these findings.

Agreement on atp1a3a/atp1a3b characterization (C80-C85). Both accept the differential effects and correction of morpholino studies. OpenEval notes contradiction with prior work; peer reviewers accept the genetic mutant data without challenge.
Agreement on atp1a3a sleep architecture (C86-C89). Both evaluations accept the detailed phenotypic characterization showing reduced bout length. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Agreement on ouabain pharmacological validation (C77-C79). Both accept the dose-response data supporting Na+/K+ pump role. OpenEval notes this addresses developmental vs. acute effects; peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Agreement on differential expression patterns (C71-C72). Both accept the data showing dmist is neuronal while fxyd1 is non-neuronal. Peer reviewer 1 notes this as raising mechanistic questions but does not challenge the data itself.
Agreement on subcellular localization (C58-C59). Both evaluations accept confocal imaging data showing differences between wild-type and mutant Dmist-GFP constructs. No concerns raised.
Agreement on circadian controls (C54, C43). Both evaluations accept that dmist expression is non-rhythmic and mutants have normal circadian period, ruling out circadian mechanisms.

Partial overlap on sodium elevation and mechanism (C12-C13). Both accept the sodium measurement data. OpenEval labels C15 as speculation requiring biochemical validation; peer reviewers accept the genetic evidence but question whether phenotypes are due to Na+ vs K+ imbalance.

Overlap on genetic interaction supporting common pathway (C14). Both evaluations accept this conclusion. OpenEval finds it well-supported by LME analysis; peer reviewers explicitly praise the epistatic analysis.

Agreement that mechanism remains uncertain (C105, C15, C70). OpenEval labels these as speculation requiring additional experiments. Peer reviewer 1 raises multiple mechanistic questions about neuronal vs extracellular Na+/K+ imbalance, indicating incomplete mechanistic resolution.

Overlap on mechanistic speculation (C111). OpenEval labels as speculation about time-of-day specific effects. Peer reviewer 1 finds the PTZ rebound difficult to understand, indicating mechanistic uncertainty.

Partial agreement on developmental vs acute effects (C106). OpenEval notes authors acknowledge they cannot exclude developmental effects in specific populations. Peer reviewers accept ouabain data as supporting acute effects but do not explicitly address remaining uncertainty.

Divergent evaluation of Na+ vs K+ mechanism (C109). OpenEval accepts the discussion of K+ as reasonable speculation based on pump function. Peer reviewer 1 explicitly raises this as a weakness, noting the authors emphasize Na+ but K+ could be equally plausible given prior shaker findings.
OpenEval evaluates background/rationale claims (C1-C2, C16-C19, C27, C30-C32) as appropriately supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory claims.
OpenEval evaluates literature summary claims (C20-C26, C28-C29, C33-C34) as accurately representing prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates C97 (speculation about undiscovered sleep genes) as appropriately labeled forward-looking statement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates discussion claims (C98-C103, C107-C108, C112-C115) as appropriate contextualization with proper citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for most discussion points, except C109 which peer reviewers questioned.
Peer reviewers accepted claims C6-C8 (additional characterization details) not explicitly grouped in OpenEval results, though these overlap with OpenEval R2-R4 coverage of molecular characterization.
Peer reviewers accepted claims C9-C10 (additional fxyd1/atp1a3a findings) not explicitly listed in OpenEval results, though conceptually covered in OpenEval R7-R8 evaluations.
